verdict: All sealed M192 arithmetic and batch identities reproduce exactly from the 120 frozen payloads, but 75,099,527 cycles is the result of retaining one flattened pair phase across token boundaries. A one-token M184-style engine should reset the pair phase at every token boundary; that exact no-reorder, one-Acc24 policy takes 71,596,122 cycles (1.108968500x versus W1), only 0.509642% slower than ideal dual-token W2. Reseal this token-flush policy and charge finite fill before RTL admission.

sealed_global_pair_phase_reproduction.production_field_name_warning: cycles_requiring_second_token_update is arithmetically fallback-minus-ideal service, not a measured temporal count from a concrete tagged response schedule
sealed_global_pair_phase_reproduction.ratio_interpretation: 1.057234941x is 5.7234941% speedup and 5.4136445% cycle reduction; it is not 57.2%.

critical_pair_phase_finding.production_policy: Flatten windows in arrival order across all tokens in one FC2 record, pair globally, fuse a pair only if both owners match, and serialize a cross-token pair without resetting phase.
critical_pair_phase_finding.problem: A serialized cross-token pair consumes the first window of the next token and prevents that window from pairing with its own following window. The 43.456046% same-token pair fraction is therefore a property of this global pair phase, not an intrinsic limit of one-context hardware.
critical_pair_phase_finding.natural_one_context_policy: Flush and restart W2 pairing at every token boundary. This preserves token order, performs no window reordering, never holds a second token context, and pairs consecutive windows within each token.
critical_pair_phase_finding.decision: Do not provision dual-token Acc24 state for the remaining 0.509642% replay gap. Reseal the token-flush point, then build the one-token pair fusion screen.

same_token_acc24_proof_boundary.reason: The windows are a partition of source events for the same FC2 token and output block. Signed weight-vector addition is associative; a cycle may select sources from either window, reduce at most one source per physical bank, and update the same Acc24 vector once.
same_token_acc24_proof_boundary.numeric_width: For binary FC2 input and signed INT8 weights, 3072*128=393216 fits signed 20 bits, so Acc24 is width-safe for the pure FC2 sum.
same_token_acc24_proof_boundary.base_context_storage_still_required: Zero extra context is relative to W1. The output-block Acc24 state itself remains external to M186 and is not charged by M192.
same_token_acc24_proof_boundary.bn_boundary: BN2, residual and ATLIF must see one final completed FC2 token value. They may not consume or commit either window as an intermediate result.

m184_m186_realizability_audit.m184_as_is_behavior: candidate_window selects one drain buffer; bank counts, event selection and release all reference only that buffer.
m184_m186_realizability_audit.functional_reuse: The two existing buffers are sufficient to hold one same-token pair. A new per-bank two-buffer selector can choose one source from either buffer while retaining one token tag and one bank read per cycle.
required_control_changes: detect a full pair or a final single-window token tail
select and decrement the correct source buffer independently for every bank
release both pair members only after their combined bank populations drain
preserve source-channel identity, output-block replay and token_done ordering
handle zero-event tokens and all 981903 token-local one-window tails
m184_m186_realizability_audit.finite_fill_risk: Pair service cannot start until the second window closes. With only two buffers, both are occupied during pair drain, so stage3 tokens with a later pair cannot overlap its fill unless a third buffer is added. Replay-only cycles do not charge this wait or producer backpressure.
m184_m186_realizability_audit.m186_limit: M186 has one outstanding in-order response and an external 2304-bit Acc24 input. It has no weight SRAM, context store, response tag or reset epoch. Its independently known stale-response reset alias must be fixed or covered by a proved flush-ack contract in the successor.

area_timing_and_memory_screen.warning: These are replay-kernel density screens only. The admission threshold must use matched finite descriptor-fill, response-latency and result-stall cycles. The nearly zero M186 setup margin makes the added per-bank selector a timing risk.
area_timing_and_memory_screen.sram_ports: Same-token fusion needs no second Acc24 port and still issues at most one read per weight bank per cycle, but its two-window source/address selector, request latency and actual bank macro timing/energy remain unmeasured.
